en: Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Gaurī said:
"O best of sages, this one is exceedingly fickle; oh, he destroys the Daityas even in his childhood! I do not know what deed he will perform hereafter."
The Daityas are of various kinds—wicked, malicious, and enemies of the virtuous gods;
therefore, for the sake of protection, you ought to bind something around his neck. || 2 ||
The Sage said:

One should meditate upon this Vināyaka, slain by a lion, with ten arms in the first age; but in the Tretā age, one should meditate upon him as having a peacock for a vehicle, with six arms, the bestower of spiritual accomplishments (siddhi).
In the Dvāpara age, however, one should meditate on the Lord Gajānana with four arms, having red unguents;
but in the fourth [age], he has two arms, is beautiful with white unguents, and always bestows all goals. || 3 ||
May Vināyaka, the Supreme Self who is higher than the highest, protect my crest-lock; may he of exceedingly beautiful body and great majesty protect my head. || 4 ||
May Kaśyapa protect my forehead; may Mahodara protect the pair of my eyebrows; may Bhālacandra protect my eyes; and may Gajānana protect my bud-like lips. (5)
May Gaṇakrīḍa protect the tongue; may the Son of Girijā protect the chin;
may Vināyaka protect the speech; and may Vighnahā protect the teeth. (6)
May Gaṇeśa, who holds a noose in his hand, protect the two ears; may he who grants the objects of one's thoughts protect the nose; and may the god Gaṇañjaya protect the mouth and the throat.
May he who has the shoulders of an elephant protect my shoulders; may the destroyer of obstacles protect my breasts;
may Gaṇanātha protect my heart, and the great Heramba my belly.
May Dhārādharā protect the sides, and may the auspicious Vighnahara protect the back;
may the mighty Vakratuṇḍa always protect the genitals and the private parts. || 9 ||
May Gaṇakrīḍa protect the knees, Maṅgalamūrtimān the thighs, Ekadanta the great intellect, and [the Lord] always protect the feet and the ankles. (10)
May the lotus-handed one, the destroyer of enemies, who swiftly inspires faith, whose arms fulfill all hopes, and whose hands, fingers, and nails protect us. 11.
May Mayūreśa, who pervades the universe, protect all my limbs forever;
and may Dhūmraketu always protect whatever place has not been mentioned.
May Āmoda protect me from the front, and may Pramoda guard me from behind;
may the Lord of Wisdom (Buddhīśa) protect me in the east, and the Bestower of Success (Siddhidāyaka) in the southeast. ||13||
May the son of Umā protect the southern direction, Gaṇeśvara the south-western,
Vighnahartā the western, and Gajakarṇaka the north-western.
May the Lord of Treasures protect [us] in the north, and the Son of Īśa in the northeast;
may Ekadanta protect by day, and Vighnahṛt during the nights and at the twilights.
May he who holds the noose and the goad protect [us] from Rākṣasas, Asuras, Vetālas, Grahas, Bhūtas, and Piśācas; may he be the mindfulness of Rajas, Sattva, and Tamas.
Knowledge, righteousness, prosperity, modesty, fame, as well as lineage, body, wealth, grain, houses, wife, sons, and friends—(all these he destroys). || 17 ||
May Mayūreśa, bearing all weapons, protect his grandsons forever;
may Kapila protect goats and the like, and may Vikaṭa protect elephants and horses.
The wise person who, having written this on birch bark, wears it around the neck, shall experience no fear from yakṣas, rākṣasas, or piśācas. (18)
Whoever recites this at the three junctions of the day shall have a body with the essence of a vajra;
whoever recites it during a journey shall obtain the fruit thereof without obstacles. (20)
Whoever recites this at the time of battle shall swiftly attain victory; it is likewise effective for the rites of killing, driving away, attracting, paralyzing, and bewildering.
If one recites this twenty-one times over seven days, the practitioner obtains those respective fruits; of this there is no doubt.
Whoever recites this twenty-one times for that many days shall immediately release from prison one who is held there, as well as one condemned to death by the king’s command. (23)
At the time of an audience with the king, one should recite this three times;
having brought the king under his influence, he shall conquer the subjects and the assembly.
This Gaṇeśa-kavaca was proclaimed by Kaśyapa to Mudgala, and by him it was then given to the great seer Māṇḍavya.
Out of compassion, he told me that armor which grants all perfections;
it should not be given to one devoid of devotion, but this auspicious [teaching] should be given to one possessed of faith.
For whomsoever this protection has been performed, no affliction shall arise anywhere for them,
whether originating from Rākṣasas, Asuras, Vetālas, Daityas, or Dānavas.
Thus ends the Gaṇeśa-kavaca in the eighty-sixth chapter of the Bālakrīḍā section of the Uttarakhaṇḍa of the glorious Gaṇeśa Purāṇa.
